rules_summary: At most one scene cut per sentence. Several cues in the same sentence (sequence + place + time) set the new scene once; they do not make several scenes.
A place change or a real time jump opens a new scene. A sequence word alone (puis, ensuite, alors, soudain / then, after that, so, suddenly) opens only a new shot in the current scene.
No cut if the place or time does not actually change (already in that room; 10:05 after 10:00).

Ignore false friends: a place only in dialogue or a memory does not cut; 'dans'/'in' without a place ('dans un silence', 'in his eyes') does not cut; glancing at a street without leaving does not cut.
A cue-only sentence with no action ('Le lendemain.', 'The next day.', 'Trois jours plus tard.') is not a scene and attaches to the next sentence.
A sentence with no action (atmosphere only) stays in the current scene and is not a required shot.
If one sentence still has two actions, the existing one-action-per-shot split applies inside the same scene.
Characters, look, outfit, place and time of day carry forward until a cue changes them. The character lock line should be copied into every shot where that character appears.

scoring.scene_boundary: An expected scene boundary is a change of place or a real time jump between two consecutive expected scenes. A found boundary is a change of place (or clearly marked time) between consecutive API scenes or shots. Correct = expected boundaries that also appear in the API output, matched by place aliases and time aliases. Missed cut = expected boundary with no matching API change. False cut = API place/scene change that does not match an expected boundary, including cuts on traps.
scoring.characters: Precision and recall against gold_characters names (case-insensitive). Spurious names (for example a parsed action fragment) are false positives. The waiter/serveur is not a gold character.
scoring.places: Precision and recall against gold_places aliases. A hit on a non_places name is a false positive.
